description: Naive / straightforward LUT replacement (paper section 4: R=512 tables, k=8, ~330.7M params). Re-scored under the FIXED validation protocol (see ../../FIXED_EVAL.md): batch size 48 x 100 eval steps, leading 12 rows skipped, batch-size-INDEPENDENT, on the held-out val shard (shard_06542.parquet) from token 0. Model rebuilt from config.json (ffn_lut_kind=fastmhl_raw, raw_n_heads=4/raw_nap=8/raw_tph=128 => R=512, k=8) and loaded from checkpoint.pt with 0 missing / 0 unexpected keys.
interpretation: Under the corrected, batch-size-independent protocol the naive LUT sits +0.0278 bpb ABOVE the matched vanilla baseline, versus the +0.0042 gap reported in the paper. The corrected protocol does not overturn the section-4 conclusion (naive LUT is not a quality win vs dense) but widens the deficit; the original small gap was flattered by the batch-coupled eval (0136 was scored at device_batch_size 12, the vanilla anchor at 48).
